header.tagline: Building intelligent systems and clear insights from data

paragraphs: I am a BIT graduate currently pursuing a Master's Degree in Information Technology with Data Analytics at the University of the West of Scotland. My work sits across AI/ML, data science, and analytics: from model-based evaluation and computer vision experiments to Python/SQL analysis, statistical testing, and dashboard storytelling. I care about results that are reproducible, honest about limitations, and useful to the people who need to act on them.

My Flutter software background gives me structured problem solving, reusable code, testing, and user-focused communication. Across my portfolio I have built PyTorch evaluation pipelines, ETL workflows, SQLite data models, exploratory analyses, KPI reports, segmentation studies, and Power BI dashboards, with clear documentation so others can follow the method as well as the headline numbers.

items.title: An Explainable VGG6 Convolutional Neural Network for Multi-Class Ovarian Cyst Classification in Ultrasound Imaging
items.citation: 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Soft Computing (CISCom 2026), Malta. Forthcoming in Springer Communications in Computer and Information Science (CCIS), Scopus-indexed.
items.summary: An explainable VGG6 CNN for multi-class ovarian cyst classification from ultrasound images, pairing deep-learning performance with interpretability to support clinical decision-making.
highlights: Designed and evaluated an explainable VGG6 architecture for multi-class ultrasound classification.
Emphasised interpretability alongside accuracy for safer clinical use of AI models.
Accepted for international oral presentation and Springer CCIS publication.

why_hire.title: Why You Should Hire Me
why_hire.intro: Five evidence-based reasons I can add value in AI/ML, data science, and analytics roles.

items.question: Why should you hire me for AI/ML, data science, or analytics roles?
items.answer: I combine model-aware thinking with software-engineering discipline and practical analytics. My portfolio spans PyTorch computer-vision evaluation, statistical analysis in Python and SQL, ETL and data-quality checks, KPI design, and dashboards that turn evidence into clear decisions. I am UK-based and ready to contribute where teams need reliable analysis and thoughtful machine learning practice.

items.question: What makes me different from a typical fresh graduate?
items.answer: Alongside my BIT degree and current Master's study in Information Technology with Data Analytics, I bring professional experience as a Flutter Developer at Gaaubesi Logistics and Thulo. That background taught me to work from requirements, debug systematically, write reusable code, test my work, use version control, and think about the person using the final product, not only the technology behind it.

items.question: How do I turn data and models into real value?
items.answer: I start with the decision or risk a stakeholder needs to manage, then choose the right level of method: exploration, statistics, dashboards, or model evaluation. My projects cover sales and retention questions as well as practical reliability in video anomaly detection, where false alerts and reviewer burden matter as much as AUC. I communicate assumptions and limitations so findings stay useful without overclaiming.

items.question: Can I work effectively with technical and non-technical teams?
items.answer: Yes. My development experience helps me collaborate on technical requirements and data workflows, while SovaVerse strengthens my ability to explain Data Science, AI, and Machine Learning concepts in approachable language. I focus on clear questions, concise visuals, documented logic, and plain-English findings so both technical colleagues and business stakeholders can follow and challenge the work.

items.question: How quickly can I learn and contribute?
items.answer: My move from mobile development into data science and machine learning shows I can transfer skills and build new capability deliberately. I have progressed from programming and databases in my BIT to applied AI/ML and analytics projects and current postgraduate study, while documenting what I learn. I contribute reliably by breaking unfamiliar problems into manageable steps, validating outputs, seeking context early, and improving through feedback.

passion.title: Making Data Science, AI & ML easier to understand
passion.lead: I believe technical knowledge becomes more valuable when it is shared clearly.
passion.body: Through SovaVerse, I explore Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Machine Learning in an approachable way, documenting my learning journey while helping others build confidence with complex ideas. I am especially passionate about practical and responsible AI: preparing reliable data, understanding how models work, and communicating what results do and do not mean.

items.name: False-Alert & Practical Reliability (Video Analytics)
description: Built a PyTorch evaluation pipeline for CUHK Avenue public-space video anomaly detection focused on false alerts and practical reliability, not only AUC.
Reported frame AUC 0.75 / AP 0.47 with event-level false alerts/hour (~20× lower than frame-level at best F1), threshold sensitivity, FP-burst analysis, and estimated reviewer minutes/hour.
Tech: Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, scikit-learn, matplotlib, SciPy

items.name: Ecommerce Transactions EDA
description: Cleaned and analyzed 6,000 synthetic transactions to assess revenue, returns, seasonality, shipping performance, and customer satisfaction.
Used chi-square, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U, and Spearman correlation to separate meaningful patterns from descriptive noise.
Found Electronics generated 42.9% of net revenue while Fashion carried the highest return burden at 20.4%.

items.name: Subscription Churn Signals
description: Analyzed retention signals across 2,200 synthetic subscribers and quantified $21.9K in monthly recurring revenue at risk.
Compared churn across contract, tenure, usage, and support-ticket segments using point-biserial correlation and bias-corrected Cramér's V.
Monthly contracts showed 28.8% churn versus 1.9% for two-year contracts, creating a clear retention hypothesis.
